Keep the Dime-Eating Tigers Out of the Foreign Settlement!

AMERICANS call them "One-arm Bandits." The Chinese have a more picturesque name—"Dime-eating Tigers." We are referring to slot-machines, a 50-year-old gambling device which has become as familiar in Shanghai as it is in certain parts of the United States, where it stands for a $50,000,000 industry. However, it is rapidly being outlawed in most states of the U.S.A.
When ratepayers of the International Settlement gathered at the Race Course last week for their annual meeting, a Russian lawyer, N. M. Shoolingin, brought forward a proposal that the Shanghai Municipal Council consider the licensing of slot-machines. One thousand machines, licensed at a fee of $100 each per month, would yield the Council a revenue of $1,200,-000 annually and help to balance the budget, he pointed out.
Slot machines are prohibited in the International Settlement and in places where they have appeared they have been seized by the police. The authorities of the neighboring French Concession enforce no such taboo and derive a handsome revenue from licensing the dime-eating tigers. No one has been able to compute the amount which goes into these machines each month and each year, but it must be enormous. The dime-eaters are to be found in bars and cabarets all over the Concession. Hundreds, if not several thousands, are in operation, and the "take" depends upon the location. In well-patronized bars, cabarets and clubs they represent an enormous business. In one cabaret in Frenchtown, five slot machines pay the entire rent of the establishment, and the "suckers" in this case are mostly taxi-dancers and their patrons.
There are several places in the International Settlement where slot-machines are operated—many of them without a formal violation of the S. M. C. edict against gambling devices. One place is a popular club operated by one of the foreign defense forces, but in this case the men made such a good deal with "Jackpot" Riley, owner and operator of most of the machines in Frenchtown, that most of the profits go toward the upkeep of the club instead of Riley. 将“吃角子老虎”拒于公共租界之外！

美国人称它们为“独臂强盗”。中国人则有一个更形象的名字——“吃角子老虎”。我们指的是老虎机，这是一种已有50年历史的赌博设备，在上海已变得如同在美国某些地区一样普遍，在那里它代表着一个价值5,000万美元的产业。然而，在美国大多数州，它正迅速被取缔。

上周，当公共租界的纳税人聚集在跑马厅参加年度会议时，一位俄罗斯律师 N. M. Shoolingin 提出了一项建议，要求上海工部局考虑对老虎机发放执照。他指出，一千台机器，每台每月收取100美元的许可费，每年可为工部局带来120万美元的收入，并有助于平衡预算。

公共租界禁止使用老虎机，在出现老虎机的地方，警方已将其没收。邻近的法租界当局并未执行此类禁令，并通过向“吃角子老虎”发放执照获得了丰厚的收入。没有人能够计算出每月和每年投入这些机器的金额，但这笔数额必定巨大。法租界各地的酒吧和歌舞厅中随处可见“吃角子老虎”。正在运行的机器有数百台，甚至可能多达数千台，其“收入”取决于地点。在顾客盈门的酒吧、歌舞厅和俱乐部中，它们代表着一项巨大的生意。在法租界的一家歌舞厅里，五台老虎机支付了该场所的全部租金，而这里的“冤大头”主要是伴舞女郎及其顾客。

在公共租界，有几个地方也在运营老虎机——其中许多并没有正式违反工部局关于禁止赌博设备的法令。其中一个地方是由某支外国防卫部队经营的一家热门俱乐部，但在这种情况下，这些人与“Jackpot” Riley（大部分法租界机器的所有者和经营者）达成了一笔非常划算的交易，使得大部分利润用于维持俱乐部的运营，而不是落入 Riley 的口袋。Riley 是一名未被承认的美国公民*，他随美国某服务机构来到远东，并在服役期满后留在此地。利用作为老虎机团伙经营者所积累的利润，他投资了其他行业，主要是餐饮和歌舞厅领域。他的企业包括位于霞飞路的一家名为“D.D.s”的俄罗斯餐厅，据说他为此支付了10,000美元。不用说，D.D's 备有大量老虎机，其嘈杂声远不利于营造让用餐者安心的氛围。

Riley 的另一项近期收购的企业是 Farren's，这是一家夜总会、餐厅和赌博场所，位于大西路附近、哥伦比亚乡村俱乐部周边的大淘（Ta-tao，音译）及日本控制区。4月22日星期一，《上海晚邮报》的一篇文章声称，美国西部著名的赌场经营者 Carlos Garcia 曾派遣一名代理人来此购买 Farren 机构，但 Jack Riley 在 Garcia 的代理人抵达前几天抢先完成了购买。

除了军人俱乐部外，公共租界内还有许多其他俱乐部和所谓的“俱乐部”及酒吧，以佣金方式运营 Riley 的老虎机。

在过去几年里，Riley 从其老虎机业务中积累了巨额财富。他的一位熟识最近估计，他从“吃角子老虎”获得的月净收入约为12,000美元，即每年150,000美元。事实上，得益于特殊情况，Riley 几乎能够“垄断”当地的老虎机市场，并建立了事实上的垄断地位。中国政府在几年前禁止进口各类赌博设备。Riley 此前已经进口了一批

NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS
MAR 1 3 1940

Municipal Lottery:
Letter in Opposition.

To the Editor of the
"North China Daily News"

Sir,—I have been surprised to see
some letters in that in a leading
article you have advocated a muni-
cipal lottery. I am sorry indeed
that in spite of the standing of the
"North China Daily News" as an
anti-gambling advocate any practice
that is generally known to be des-
tructive of good morals.

A lottery is gambling. Gambling
is a crime. Were the Municipality to
establish a lottery, it would not only
legalize a crime, but would, by
giving its sanction in crime—would
encourage crime.

On what ground can a dis-
tinction be drawn between the
gambling dens of the Western and
other parts of Shanghai and a
gambling den municipally conducted?
One would have more respect for the
unscrupulous keepers of those vile
places than the police have been
trying faithfully and manfully to
drive out of our city, than for the
city which so far lowers itself as
to establish a lottery. Should it be
said that great nations have con-
ducted lotteries, it can only be said
that in so doing no nation has shown
itself great; and the object of one's
respect would not be altered because
the gamblers had larger proportions.
At one time one state of the United
States of America conducted a
lottery. It became a curse to the
entire nation, until finally, by
Federal Statute, it was outlawed
from use of the mails.

Those who buy lottery tickets, in
the main, are the poor—the clerk,
the stenographer, the men and
women with small incomes, who
spend their little all on the hope
of winning a fortune at a stroke.
The expenses of the government of
right should in the main be borne by
the rich. But through the lottery as
an instrument of government, it
would fall on the poor. Of these
poor, only a few, a very, very few,
get something back. The large
majority lose all. And when the
loser there has lost all of his own
money, he becomes under the great
temptation to steal from to embezzle
the money of his employer.

Good government values the
morals of the people at higher worth
than money, and good government
cannot teach the people crime.

Chas. W. Martin.
Shanghai, Mar. 18.

致《字林西报》编辑先生

先生，——我惊讶地看到，在贵报一篇社论中，竟主张发行市政彩票。鉴于《字林西报》素以倡导禁赌著称，而赌博这一行为众所周知会败坏良好道德，对此我深感遗憾。

彩票即赌博。赌博是犯罪。若工部局设立彩票，不仅会使犯罪行为合法化，更会因官方对犯罪的认可而助长犯罪风气。

有何理由将上海西区及其他地区的私人赌窟与市政经营的赌窟加以区分？对于那些卑劣场所肆无忌惮的经营者，警方一直忠实且勇敢地试图将其驱逐出本市；相比之下，人们反而会对一个自降身份至设立彩票的城市给予更多尊重吗？若有人辩称大国曾发行过彩票，只能说明此举并未彰显任何国家的伟大；即便赌徒规模更大，也不应成为受人尊敬的理由。美国曾有一个州发行过彩票。这成了整个国家的祸害，直到最终通过联邦法令，禁止利用邮政系统从事此类活动。

购买彩票者主要为穷人——职员、速记员以及收入微薄的男女，他们将微薄的积蓄全部押注于指望一夜暴富的希望之上。正当政府的开支主要应由富人承担。但若通过彩票作为政府筹资手段，负担将落在穷人身上。在这些穷人中，只有极少数，非常非常少的人能有所回报。绝大多数人血本无归。而当输家输光自己的钱后，在巨大的诱惑下，他便会去偷窃或侵吞雇主的钱财。

良政视人民道德重于金钱，良政不能教导人民犯罪。

查尔斯·W·马丁 (Chas. W. Martin)
上海，3月18日

between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m.

Double Aid

Men put on the Chaoufoong
Road list have been taken off the
Headquarters roster, said the
Brigadier. He had found that
some men obtaining relief at the
shelter were also going up to
Headquarters and getting a hand-
out there.

Brigadier Morris also revealed
that he was now using Chinese
bed coverlets at the shelter in-
stead of blankets. Out of 100
bought last year, no less than 70
have been stolen by conscience-
less inmates (not that all of them
would do such a thing, he added).

Windows Closed

He has had to close all shelter
windows opening on to the main
road because he has found that
some of the inmates have been
throwing blankets out to accom-
plices on the road. Sheets have
been stolen, wrapped around the
body of an inmate under his
shirt. Knives and forks disap-
pear rapidly.

Work on fixing up the build-
ing (in which the PWD has
helped greatly) should bring it
into good shape in another fort-
night, the Brigadier said. This
work included a bath house. At
present inmates who asked for
baths were given money to pay
for them elsewhere.

1940年3月12日

救世军收容所住客
抱怨总体状况

莫里斯少校解释赵丰路（音译）工作尚未完成；问题住客偷窃毯子、床单、刀叉

寄给《上海晚邮报》的关于赵丰路（音译）救世军收容所住客的投诉显示，这些新住所亟需改善，另一方面，有关方面正努力进行整改。

部分投诉似乎基于这样一个事实：该场所在尚未完全准备就绪时便被接管，目前仍处于过渡状态。莫里斯少校解释了救世军将被重振的政策细节。

**〔此处转录不清〕**

前往收容所的访客以及上海救世军指挥官莫里斯少校均承认，该场所目前尚不完全令人满意，但表示这与最近腾退的许多旧处所相比已有显著改善。

莫里斯少校指出，收容所接收了许多粗鲁的顾客，这些人习惯粗野且肮脏。救世军尽力照顾他们，秉持他们是人类、需要食物和住所的观点，但他们确实需要大量的照料。

较优类型人员

目前在赵丰路（音译），美国和英国籍住客被安置在两间宿舍中的一间，其他国籍男子则住在第二间。救世军关于宿舍的政策是，同一房间居住人数越多越好，因此计划采用大寝室而非小房间。

莫里斯少校称，救世军接收任何申请进入收容所的男子。较优类型的人员被安置在扬子饭店（Yang Tze Hostel），仅在其习惯不良时才被要求离开。

食物投诉

莫里斯少校表示，在过渡期间，赵丰路（音译）处不收取食物费用。他还指出，当被问及关于食物的投诉时，救世军并未拒绝向未提出请求的人提供食物。当该场所运行时

目前仅向年长住客提供午餐。“我们为何要鼓励身强力壮或年轻的男子整天无所事事地在附近游荡？”莫里斯少校说。“这并非收容所的初衷。”除体弱者外，住客必须在上午8点至下午5点之间离开该场所。

双重援助

莫里斯少校称，列入赵丰路（音译）名单的人员已从总部名册中除名。他发现，一些在收容所获得救济的男子同时也前往总部并在那里领取施舍。

莫里斯少校还透露，他现在在收容所使用中式床罩而非毯子。去年购买的100条毯子中，不少于70条被没有良心的住客偷走（他补充说，并非所有人都会做这种事）。

关闭窗户

他不得不关闭所有朝向主干道的收容所窗户，因为他发现一些住客将毯子扔给路上的同伙。床单也被偷走，方法是将其缠在住客衬衫下的身体上。刀叉迅速消失。

少校表示，修缮建筑的工作（工务处在此方面提供了极大帮助）应在另外两周内使其达到良好状态。这项工作包括建造一间浴室。目前，要求洗澡的住客会获发钱款以便在其他地方付费洗澡。

THE CHINA PRESS, WEDNESDAY, JULY 8, 1936

Police Make
New Raids For
Slot Machines

Operators Of Mechanical Robbers Face
Prosecution

Some people engaged in the bar and restaurant business evidently didn't believe the police when the latter conducted a wholesale roundup of slot machines operating in the International Settlement several months ago. Either that, or they thought the police had forgotten.

The police had not forgotten and more than that, they meant exactly what they said. During the past few days they have rounded up five more slot machines in several places in the Central District. These machines, it was revealed, had been in operation for a few weeks and their operators had ignored warnings issued to have them removed.

At the present time, the police have the machines in custody and will probably use them as evidence against the owners in court at some future date.

The cleanup campaign against slot machines in the Settlement started last year when police issued warnings to all bars and restaurants where the mechanical robbers were in operation to have them removed. The majority responded to the warning but several did not with the result that they found themselves in court.

Convictions were handed down against practically all persons prosecuted by the police and fines were meted out with warnings that the machines would be confiscated if they were put back into operation.

With several months gone by, a few machines began to reappear a few weeks ago. Police were informed of this breach of regulations and immediately checked up on the reports. They found some of them true and issued warnings to have the machines removed. A few were removed. Five didn't and the machines were seized.

警方再次

显然，几个月前警方在国际租界对运营中的老虎机进行大规模围剿时，一些从事酒吧和餐馆生意的人并不相信警方。要么是这样，要么他们认为警方已经忘记了此事。

警方并未忘记，不仅如此，他们的言行一致。在过去几天里，他们在中区多处又查获了五台老虎机。据悉，这些机器已运营数周，其操作者无视移除警告。

目前，警方已扣押这些机器，并可能在未来的某个日期在法庭上将其作为针对业主的证据。

针对租界内老虎机的清理运动始于去年，当时警方警告所有运营这种“机械强盗”的酒吧和餐馆将其移除。大多数人都响应了警告，但有几家没有，结果发现自己被告上法庭。

几乎所有被警方起诉的人都被判有罪，并被处以罚款，同时受到警告：如果重新投入运营，机器将被没收。

几个月过去了，几周前一些机器开始重新出现。警方获悉这一违规行为并立即核实报告。他们发现部分报告属实，并发出警告要求移除机器。少数机器被移除。有五家未予理会，机器遂被查获。

THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, JULY 11, 1936

Slot Machine
Magnate Is
Fined $100

5 Mechanical Robbers
Confiscated By
Swiss Court

WIDLER DOES NOT
CONTEST ACTION

Machines Operated
Despite S.M.C.
Ban

Mr. Elly Widler, slot-machine magnate in the International Settlement, was fined $100 and five slot machines were confiscated by Mr. E. Lardy, Swiss Consul-General, in the Swiss Consular Court yesterday.

Widler appeared in court in answer to a police summons charging him with operating slot machines for gambling purposes in his shop on Central Road known as the Machine Exchange.

Police were informed during the latter part of May that Widler had machines in operation despite municipal regulations banning the "mechanical robbers" from the Settlement.

Investigation of the report was made, and according to Detective Inspector Telfer, of the Central Station, it was found to be true. On June 11, Inspector Telfer continued in outlining the case, the police, acting on a search warrant, raided Widler's establishment and seized the machines.

When asked if he had anything to say about the case, Widler declared that he would not contest the action of the police, thereby saving something in court costs. He was fined $100 and Mr. Lardy ordered the five machines confiscated in the name of the state.

Inspector Telfer asked Mr. Lardy what was meant by confiscation of the machines "in the name of the state." He continued that it was his impression that when gambling machines were seized, they were destroyed after conviction had been handed down by the court.

Mr. Lardy explained that under Swiss law, property ordered confiscated by the court was sold and the money received was used for charitable purposes or for other funds. He stated that in the case of the slot machines, the court might dispose of them in areas where they were permitted.

There was some further discussion on the matter with the result that Mr. Lardy finally agreed to refer the matter to the Commissioner of Police.

老虎机
大亨被

五台“机械强盗”
被瑞士法庭
没收

维德勒未对
该行动提出抗辩

尽管工部局
禁止，机器仍
在运营

公共租界的老虎机大亨埃利·维德勒（Elly Widler）先生昨日在瑞士领事法庭被瑞士总领事E.拉迪（E. Lardy）先生罚款100美元，并没收五台老虎机。

维德勒出庭应诉警方传票，指控他在位于中央路（Central Road）、名为“机器交易所”（Machine Exchange）的店铺内运营用于赌博目的的老虎机。

警方在五月底获悉，尽管市政法规禁止这些“机械强盗”进入租界，维德勒仍在运营其机器。

经对该报告进行调查，据中央捕房督察特尔弗（Telfer）称，调查结果属实。6月11日，特尔弗督察在概述案情时继续指出，警方依据搜查令突袭了维德勒的场所并查获了这些机器。

当被问及是否对此案有何陈述时，维德勒声明他不会对警方的行动提出抗辩，从而节省了一些诉讼费用。他被罚款100美元，拉迪先生下令以国家名义没收这五台机器。

特尔弗督察询问拉迪先生，以“国家名义”没收机器是何含义。他接着说，他的印象是，当赌博机器被查获后，会在法院宣判定罪后予以销毁。

拉迪先生解释说，根据瑞士法律，法院命令没收的财产将被出售，所得款项用于慈善事业或其他基金。他表示，就老虎机而言，法院可能会在允许使用此类机器的地区处理它们。

对此事又进行了一些讨论，结果拉迪先生最终同意将此事宜转交警务处处长。

THE CHINA PRESS, FRIDAY, FEBRUARY 14, 〔此处转录不清〕
B. D. 27c8

New Nickle Subsidiary Coins
Just Fit Local Slot Machines

Mechanical Gambling Device Owners In French
Concession Take New Heart With
Pleasing Recent Discovery

The new coins being minted by the National Government and now in circulation will not affect the slot machine business or "racket." On the contrary, the new coins should improve things for the owners of the mechanical gambling machines.

Considerable fear was thrown into the minds of slot machine operators in Shanghai when the new coins put in their appearance. A rumor got around that the new 20-cent pieces wouldn't fit the slots in the machines and for a time, the situation looked dark indeed.

A China Press reporter went out and investigated yesterday morning and on testing five different machines, all of which took the old 20-cent piece, found that the new coin fitted perfectly, in fact they fitted much better than the old coins.

The story was a bit different with the table games, which operate on the slot system, to be found around the city. The new 20-cent coins cannot be used in operating these games, or at least they can't be used in most of them. There may be a few exceptions to the rule but if so, The China Press investigator didn't find any and he tried three different kinds of table games.

Jack Pot Machines Okeh

The jackpot machines, however, are okeh. There are three types of these machines in Shanghai, one built to take the U.S. dollar, the second for the U.S. 25-cent piece and the third for U.S. nickel coin. The dollar machines are relatively few and since the nationalization of silver, they were practically pushed out of business.

The machines using the American quarter or 25-cent have always been more numerous and far more popular with the gambling element. They were found to take the local 20-cent piece and for years such machines have been found in all parts of the city; that is they were found in all parts of the city until a few months ago when all slot-machines except table games were banned from the International Settlement. There are still plenty of them in the French Concession.

These are the machines which all the worry and bother was over when the new 20-cent piece made its appearance. Operators saw themselves having to go to all the trouble of having brass slugs made in order to operate their machines, and this method is never exactly satisfactory, they explain. The use of the actual coin is always more profitable than the slug for when a person has the actual coin, he is far more apt to play a machine than he would be if he had to purchase slugs. Although more awkward to handle, cold cash always looks better in the middle of a poker table than a pile of chips, and silver always looks better in a slot machine jackpot than brass.

Worry Needless

All this worry about having to buy slugs was needless. The new coin is apparently the exact size of an American quarter whereas the old 20-cent piece was slightly thinner. This thinness in the old coin was not so good for the machine operators for the simple reason that when a machine did pay out, it was inclined to give the player bigger dividends than those prescribed.

For instance, on some machines, when a dividend of four coins was won, the old 20-cent piece would cause five coins to be dropped out. If eight coins was to be the dividend, it was not unusual for 10 to drop out. Of course, the operator usually got it all back anyway and he really had no kick coming. Still, he kicked. The new coin, however, should give no reason for complaint, for with it the machine drops out the prescribed dividend, neither more nor less.

Regarding the third type of machine, there are quite a few in Shanghai. They have, in the past, been operated on the slug system, each slug being worth 40 cents. The new 10-cent coin, however, which is approximately the size of an American nickel, fits this type of machine exactly and pays out the prescribed dividend, if and when one is prescribed.

Yes, slot machine operators should be able to rest easy from now on; that is unless the French police decide to close down on them.

《字林西报》，〔此处转录不清〕2月14日，星期五
B. D. 27c8

新镍质辅币
恰好适配本地老虎机

法租界的机械赌博设备业主因
近期的可喜发现而
重拾信心

国民政府正在铸造并现已流通的新硬币不会影响老虎机业务或“非法勾当”。相反，新硬币应当改善机械赌博机业主的经营状况。

当新硬币出现时，上海的老虎机经营者心中产生了相当大的恐惧。有谣言称，新的20分硬币无法放入机器的投币口，有一段时间，形势确实看起来很不妙。

《字林西报》记者昨天上午外出调查，在测试了五台不同的机器后——这些机器均接受旧的20分硬币——发现新硬币完全适配，事实上比旧硬币更贴合。

遍布全市、采用投币系统运行的桌面游戏情况则略有不同。新的20分硬币不能用于操作这些游戏，或者至少不能用于大多数此类游戏。也许有个别例外，但如果有，《字林西报》的调查员并未发现，他尝试了三种不同类型的桌面游戏。

头奖机器没问题

然而，头奖机器（Jack Pot Machines）没有问题。上海有三种此类机器，一种设计为接受美国一元硬币，第二种接受美国25分硬币，第三种接受美国5分镍币。一元硬币机器相对较少，自白银国有化以来，它们实际上已被挤出市场。

使用美国25分硬币的机器一直数量更多，且在赌博人群中更受欢迎。人们发现这些机器可以接受本地20分硬币，多年来在全市各地都能见到此类机器；也就是说，直到几个月前，除桌面游戏外，所有老虎机在公共租界被禁之前，它们遍布全市各处。在法租界，这类机器仍然很多。

当新的20分硬币出现时，所有的担忧和麻烦都围绕着这些机器。经营者看到自己不得不费尽周折去定制黄铜代币以运行他们的机器，他们解释说，这种方法从来都不尽如人意。使用真币总是比使用代币更有利可图，因为当一个人持有真币时，他更有可能去玩机器，而如果必须购买代币，这种可能性就会降低。虽然处理起来较为笨拙，但在扑克桌中间，冷冰冰的现金总比一堆筹码好看；而在老虎机的头奖中，银币总是比黄铜好看。

担忧实属多余

所有关于必须购买代币的担忧都是多余的。新硬币的尺寸显然与美国25分硬币完全相同，而旧的20分硬币则稍薄一些。旧硬币的这种薄度对机器经营者来说并不好，原因很简单，当机器派彩时，它倾向于支付给玩家比规定更多的红利。

例如，在某些机器上，当赢得四枚硬币的红利时，旧的20分硬币会导致吐出五枚硬币。如果红利应为八枚硬币，吐出十枚也不罕见。当然，经营者通常无论如何都能把多出的部分赚回来，所以他其实没什么可抱怨的。尽管如此，他还是抱怨了。然而，新硬币应该没有理由让人抱怨，因为使用它时，机器吐出的红利既不多也不少，正好符合规定。

关于第三种类型的机器，上海也有不少。过去，它们一直通过代币系统运行，每个代币价值40分。然而，新的10分硬币尺寸大约相当于美国5分镍币，恰好适配这种类型的机器，并在有规定红利的情况下，准确支付规定的红利。

是的，老虎机经营者从现在起应该可以高枕无忧了；除非法国警察决定对他们进行取缔。

THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY, AUGUST 4, 1935 SHANGHAI

Court Exacts
Big Fine For
Slot Machine

Police Campaign Against
Gambling Devices Gets
Emphatic Legal Support

Restaurant Owner Is
Ordered To Pay $200

The First Special District Court yesterday morning gave strong support to the campaign of the police to ban the slot machine from the International Settlement by imposing a fine of $200 upon one offender, or giving him the alternative of spending 100 days at hard labor.

The offender was a restaurant owners named Tang Wei-ju, of 165 Honan Road. He was summoned to appear before the court after a visit from the police more than a week ago. A slot machine was found on the premises, operating in direct contravention to police orders. The authorities seized the machine and brought it into court as evidence against the accused.

Police charged that the slot machine was nothing more than a gambling device and that Tang had left it in operation in his place after he had been told to take it out. The accused denied that it was a gambling machine, but that it was a merchandise vendor.

If the restaurant proprietor had any idea that the court would let him off with a small fine of two or three dollars, as has been the case in the past, he was rudely disappointed. The court sided with the police in their efforts to get the slot machines out of the Settlement and handed down punishment accordingly. The man was warned that things would go even harder with him, if he repeated the offense.

This marks the second time in little more than a month that an offender against police instructions to remove slot machines from public places has been brought before the First Special District Court. The first offender, who also used the defense that the machine was a merchandise vendor and hence could not be classified as a gambling device, was let off with a warning and a fine of $2.

Present serious campaign of the police against the "slot" machines started about two months ago when all machines in public places were ordered removed by the authorities. Orders were issued to their owners or operators to remove them before a certain date. The majority complied with the order and as a result, slot machines are rare in the Settlement and a drug on the market in every other section in the city. It was estimated that before the campaign these machines, of which there were more than 1,000 in the three municipalities, took in an annual harvest of more than $3,500,000.

《字林西报》，1935年8月4日，星期日，上海

法庭对
老虎机案件
处以重罚

警方打击
赌博设备的行动获得
有力的法律支持

餐馆老板被
责令支付200美元

第一特区地方法院昨日上午通过对一名违法者处以200美元罚款，或 alternatively 判处100天苦役，有力地支持了警方禁止老虎机进入公共租界的行动。

违法者是河南路165号的一家餐馆老板，名叫唐伟儒（Tang Wei-ju，音译）。在一周多前警方走访后，他被传唤出庭。在该场所发现了一台正在运行的老虎机，直接违反了警方命令。当局扣押了该机器并将其作为指控被告的证据带入法庭。

警方指控该老虎机无非是一种赌博设备，且唐某在被告知将其移除后，仍让其留在店内运行。被告否认它是赌博机，辩称它是一种商品售货机。

如果这位餐馆老板以为法院会像过去那样只让他缴纳两三美元的小额罚款了事，那他就大错特错了。法院站在警方一边，支持他们将老虎机清除出租界的努力，并据此作出了处罚。此人受到警告，如果再犯，处境将更加艰难。

这是在短短一个多月的时间里，第二次有违反警方移除公共场所老虎机指令的违法者被带上第一特区地方法庭。第一名违法者也以该机器是商品售货机、因此不能归类为赌博设备为由进行辩护，最终仅受到警告并被罚款2美元。

警方目前针对“老虎”机器的严肃行动始于大约两个月前，当时当局命令移除公共场所的所有机器。已向业主或经营者发出命令，要求他们在特定日期前移除机器。大多数人遵守了命令，因此，老虎机在租界内已属罕见，在全市其他区域也滞销。据估计，在这次行动之前，这三个市政区共有1000多台此类机器，每年的收入超过350万美元。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, MONDAY, JULY 8, 1935

SLOT MACHINES AND SLUGS OVERBOARD
New York Police Renew Their Anti-Gambling Activity

Far from the haunts of racketeers and counterfeit coin passers, 4,000 firearms of various types and sizes, two tons of slugs ($32,650 worth to subway turnstile cheaters) and 450 slot machines were carried 45 miles up Long Island Sound, New York, recently, and dumped in 150 feet of water at a point two and a half miles off Eaton Neck.

The slot machines and the weapons, which included about 200 knives, blackjacks, brass knuckles and sabres, had been seized in police raids, most of them during the past year. The slugs, turned over to the Police Department by the Board of Transportation, represented the intake of spurious coins by the independent Subway System since it opened on Sept. 10, 1932. The slugs had been dropped into the turnstiles at the rate of 1,787 daily over this period.

Mayor LaGuardia, Police Commissioner Valentine and the District Attorney of three counties were present at Pier A at the Battery when the contraband was loaded upon two city-owned tugs. The Mayor, chipper in manner and wearing a dark blue suit and a Panama hat, made a brief speech in which he issued a warning to "tin horn gangsters and racketeers" that no quarter would be shown them.

Promises Rough Treatment

Waving a pistol in his hand as he stood beside two cases of revolvers and a load of slot machines, the Mayor said:

"Here you see a splendid exhibition of police energy. The Police Department, with the co-operation of the five District Attorneys has been able to put the fear of the Lord into the gangsters. Let this be a notice to them that they will be treated just as roughly as we are going to treat these implements."

Then the Mayor took a sledgehammer and swung it lustily five times over a slot machine, before turning the heavy tool over to the Commissioner to complete the task.

Mr. LaGuardia also stated that he had instructed Licence Commissioner Paul Moss to cease issuing licences for the pin or bagatelle game, which caused the conviction in the courts of a stationery-store proprietor for maintaining a gambling room. His order to the commissioner, the Mayor added, would hold unless the Court of Appeals rules the decision invalid or the city is served with a mandamus order.

Wants Laws Tightened

In a talk with newspaper and newsreel men the Mayor called for Congressional action to tighten laws to prohibit the transportation of firearms from one State to another. All the guns on the boats, Mr. LaGuardia said he was told, were brought here from other States.

"Most of the punks who owned these guns are up the river now. Let's keep up the good work and make New York a better place to live in," the Mayor concluded.

Commissioner Valentine spoke in favour of a "Federal Sullivan Law," which would prevent the sale of firearms to individuals in near-by States and stop their transportation here. He said a recent murder of a police officer was due to the laxity of the laws of a neighbouring State.

Commissioner Valentine, District Attorneys Dodge of New York, Geoghan of Brooklyn and Walsh of Staten Island sailed into Long Island Sound with the cargo before stopping at Stepping Stone Light, off City Island, where they threw the weapons and machines into the water for the benefit of camera men on board.

The commissioner, starting with a machine gun, held the weapons up, explaining the construction, and heaved them into the Sound. The District Attorneys joined him in tossing weapons over the side of the boat. "If anybody can get them back," the commissioner commented "they're welcome to them."

Fifteen Police Department employees and three men from the Board of Transportation assisted in loading the seized materials aboard the Manhattan and the Sixty-nine of the Department of Docks, which left the Battery at 11.30 a.m. The return trip required nine hours.

《字林西报》，1935年7月8日，星期一

老虎机与假币投入海中
纽约警方重启反赌博行动

远离敲诈勒索者和使用假币者的巢穴，4,000支各种类型和尺寸的枪支、两吨重用于欺骗地铁旋转栅门的假币（价值32,650美元）以及450台老虎机，近日被运至纽约长岛湾上游45英里处，并在距伊顿颈（Eaton Neck）两英里半的地方倾倒入150英尺深的水中。

这些老虎机和武器（包括约200把刀、短棍、指节铜套和马刀）均是在警方突袭行动中缴获的，其中大部分是在过去一年内查获的。这批假币由运输局移交给警察局，代表了独立地铁系统自1932年9月10日开通以来收到的伪币收入。在此期间，每天投入旋转栅门的假币数量达1,787枚。

拉瓜迪亚市长、警察局长瓦伦丁以及三个县的地区检察官均在巴特利区的A码头现场监督违禁品装上两艘市政府拥有的拖船。市长精神抖擞，身着深蓝色西装，头戴巴拿马草帽，发表了简短讲话，警告“虚张声势的匪徒和敲诈者”，表示绝不会对他们手软。

扬言严厉处置

市长站在两箱左轮手枪和一批老虎机旁，手中挥舞着一把手枪说道：

“你们在这里看到了警方活力的精彩展示。警察局在五位地区检察官的配合下，已使匪徒们心生敬畏。以此通知他们，我们将像处理这些器具一样，对他们采取同样严厉的手段。”

随后，市长拿起一把大锤，在一台老虎机上用力挥击了五次，然后将这件沉重的工具交给警察局长以完成销毁工作。

拉瓜迪亚先生还表示，他已指示执照专员保罗·莫斯（Paul Moss）停止颁发用于玩弹珠或巴加特尔游戏（pin or bagatelle game）的执照，此前一名文具店店主因开设赌博场所而被法院定罪。市长补充说，除非上诉法院裁定该判决无效，或者市政府收到强制令，否则他对专员的命令将一直有效。

要求收紧法律

在与报纸记者和新闻片摄影师的谈话中，市长呼吁国会采取行动，收紧法律，禁止跨州运输枪支。拉瓜迪亚先生说，据他得知，船上的所有枪支都是从其他州运来的。

“拥有这些枪支的小混混们现在大多已在狱中服刑。让我们继续保持良好势头，使纽约成为一个更适宜居住的地方，”市长总结道。

瓦伦丁局长赞成制定一部“联邦沙利文法”，以防止向邻近各州的个人出售枪支并阻止将其运入本市。他表示，最近发生的一起谋杀警察案件是由于邻州法律松懈所致。

瓦伦丁局长、纽约区检察官多奇（Dodge）、布鲁克林区检察官乔汉（Geoghan）以及斯塔滕岛区检察官沃尔什（Walsh）随货物乘船进入长岛湾，在城岛（City Island）附近的踏脚石灯塔（Stepping Stone Light）停泊，为了供船上的摄影师拍摄，他们将武器和机器投入水中。

局长从一挺机枪开始，举起武器解释其构造，然后将其扔进海湾。各区检察官也加入了他，将武器从船边抛下。“如果有人能把它们捞回来，”局长评论道，“那就送给他们吧。”

十五名警察局雇员和三名运输局人员协助将缴获物资装上码头局的“曼哈顿号”和“六十九号”船只，这两艘船于上午11时30分离开巴特利区。返程耗时九小时。

（手写签名：7月10日）

《上海泰晤士报》，7月某日，星期五

特区法院禁止老虎机

查获该机器的餐馆老板依中国刑法被判无罪，但依警章被判有罪并受告诫

近期由助理市政检察官T. S. Lea发起的针对国际租界内老虎机的警方行动中的首个测试案件，昨日在第一特区法院顺利审结。查获该机器的餐馆老板虽依据《中华民国刑法》第280条关于容留及提供场所供公众赌博的规定被判无罪，但依据《特别警察律》第45条第1款被判有罪并受到告诫。被没收的老虎机责令归还给他，但命令不得再次安装。

在周一于中国法庭进行的长时间听证会上，辩方和控方就老虎机是否属于赌博装置进行了辩论。控方由助理市政检察官T. S. Lea担任，而被告一方则有多位法律人才出庭辩护。被告为席昆松（Hsi Kwen-sung，音译）先生，50岁，系河南路165/7号一家餐馆的老板，该处即查获机器的地点。他被指控“容留并提供场所供公众赌博。违反《中华民国刑法》第280条及《特别警察律》第45条第1款”。

老虎机在法庭上出示并在王法官面前运行。三十枚代币被插入机器，而机器仅回吐了约三分之一的数量，从而显示业主获得了66%的利润。然而，辩方的主张是，该机器售卖糖果卷。

尽管玩家获得的回报很少，表明该装置具有巨大的优势，但该机器也有一个可取之处。它确实会吐出糖果卷，当然前提是必须转动附在机器上的糖果容器底部的一个小手柄。任何不知道这个手柄的人都不会得到糖果。

只要玩家转动那个小手柄，机器确实会释放出一卷糖果，这一事实为辩方提供了有力的辩护理由。控方辩称，糖果仅仅是一种“诱饵”，而机器在游玩时会退还代币，且这些代币可兑换现金或赊账额度，这使得它成为一种赌博装置。

昨日，王法官依据《刑法》第280条宣告席先生刑事罪名不成立，并命令将其移交违例法庭，就违例指控进行审判。

违例法庭宋法官判其有罪，对其予以告诫，并命令将机器归还给他，但不得再次安装在餐馆内。

THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY, JUNE 23, 1935

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY.
No. D 2708
Date 24 / 6 / 35

Comprehensive Drive On City's
Slot Machines Gains Impetus

Cleanup Started Two Weeks Ago Checked Up By
Police; Prosecutions Face Offenders After
New Check-Up Tomorrow; Huge Profits Made

That old familiar mechanical robber, the slot machine, is to be banished from the International Settlement. He has already received his walking papers, and while his window is still shining in dark streets, a good many of his kind have already read the handwriting on the wall and have gone into retirement in attics, backrooms and godowns.

The cleanup of the slot machines started two weeks ago when members of the Intelligence Squad, Central Station, made the rounds of the district; and notified restaurant and cafe owners who had a mechanical chiseler in their establishment to remove him forthwith or take the consequences.

Chief Inspector F. C. Stephens of the Central Station, who has charge of the cleanup in his district, told a China Press reporter yesterday that all owners of machines had been notified, and that a check had revealed that the most reputable concerns had complied with the order.

A further check will be made shortly, and it is understood that those who have disobeyed will probably face prosecution. Some prosecutions have already been started, it is reported.

The cleanup spread from the Central Station to other police stations in the Settlement, and it is reported that efforts to put down on the slot machine have been fairly successful in all areas.

Questioned as to whether shops that were being cleared of these machines that were vendors of merchandise such as gum and mints, police stated that in the present cleanup all machines are to go. While it has been the policy of the Settlement authorities in the past to permit machines which dispensed articles of value instead of money, the painted fruit machines and similar devices which give a player a chance to win a piece of gum or mint with each coin played in the slot, have become more than just a harmless bit of fun. They are the real thing, being in effect that can be turned into cash at the counter.

**Profitable Racket**

That a huge sum is taken by slot machines in Shanghai every year is not a myth. Police estimates place the number in the International Settlement at around 300, and then say that this is a conservative figure. It is estimated that these machines take in approximately $1,000,000 a year, half of which goes into the pockets of the men who own the machines, while the other half goes to the restaurant, bar or cabaret owner.

In the French Concession, Settlement and Chinese areas, it is calculated that there are approximately 1,000 machines in operation taking more than $4,000,000 annually. In other words, the slot machine has developed into one of the biggest rackets in the city, taking in more money every day for the operators than the old Gambling Hell House roulette wheel owned by Carlos Garcia.

Most of the machines in Shanghai are owned by syndicates or individuals. Many small fry own three or four machines which they place in bars, restaurants and cabarets. Even with only this small number of machines, one man can make a comfortable income, running well above $1,000 a month. One individual in the city owns a string of 72 machines and his average take on a machine is $100 monthly, giving him an income of more than $10,000. In pre-Shanghai depression days, his monthly take would run to $20,000 a month.

The Chinese Maritime Customs took the attitude that the slot machine was nothing more or less than a mechanical thief some four or five years ago and banned the importation of such games. At that time, there were only about 50 machines in the entire city. Since then, the number has swollen to a thousand, or possibly more. The police use that figure as a minimum.

**Machines Smuggled In**

From this it appears that the business of smuggling machines into China has been a lucrative one for somebody. To make the cleanup more interesting, there are business concerns in Shanghai today dealing in slot machines quite openly, getting big prices for their goods and finding a ready market for them.

These concerns, while they will place a machine in a restaurant on a fifty-fifty basis, prefer to sell them outright for the profit is quick and the turnover big. Most of the machines that are on the market in Shanghai today cost from $600 to $1,000. The total investment in these machines in the city is estimated at about $700,000.

Slot machines of the American variety first made their appearance in Shanghai in a big way in the winter of 1928 and 1929. There were a few in the Settlement and Concession prior to that time but these could be counted on the fingers of both hands. They were owned by a few individual bar owners and were played for cigars and other merchandise.

The first public service as Shanghai knows it was made in late 1928 when a big slot machine man from the United States arrived in his appearance in this port with 18 machines and proceeds to take orders on them for a company in New York. This man had been operating in Europe prior to his coming to the Orient, and had found the countries of the continent were definitely opposed to slot machines. After a bitter experience in Switzerland which landed him in jail for a brief spell and almost resulted in the confiscation of his machines, he set out for Shanghai.

He found this city a good place for his particular line of endeavor and before many months had passed had increased his field of machines to two dozen. A trip he made to Canton and Tientsin supplied the majority of the machines needed for the Chinese cities. As a result of his activities, the result was that the machines went into action.

How extensive the present racket actually is could not be learned yesterday. I have been told that there are still many machines on premises. It is not known what steps will be taken to force dealers to remove the machines in the near future. Getting the machines off the street is one problem; getting rid of the gambling element under the wheel at 134-O Bubbling Well Road is another.

《字林西报》，1935年6月23日，星期日

上海公共租界工部局警务处
特别分部登记处。
编号 D 2708
日期 1935年6月24日

全市老虎机大扫除行动势头增强

清理工作于两周前开始，由警方进行检查；明日再次检查后将对违规者提起诉讼；利润巨大

那个古老而熟悉的机械强盗——老虎机，即将被逐出公共租界。它已经收到了驱逐令，虽然它的橱窗在黑暗的街道上依然闪亮，但许多同类已经看到了不祥之兆，纷纷退隐至阁楼、后屋和仓库中。

对老虎机的清理工作始于两周前，当时中央捕房情报股的警员巡视了辖区，并通知那些店内设有这种“机械扒手”的餐馆和咖啡馆老板，要么立即将其移除，要么承担后果。

负责其辖区清理工作的中央捕房总督察 F. C. Stephens（音译）昨日告诉《字林西报》记者，所有机器所有者均已收到通知，且检查显示，声誉良好的商号已遵守命令。

不久将进行进一步检查，据悉，那些违抗命令的人可能会面临起诉。据报道，一些诉讼程序已经启动。

清理工作已从中央捕房扩展到租界内的其他巡捕房，据报道，在各区域打击老虎机的努力都相当成功。

当被问及那些正在清除这些机器的商店是否是口香糖和薄荷糖等商品的销售商时，警方表示，在本次清理行动中，所有机器都必须移除。虽然过去租界当局的政策是允许那些分发有价值物品而非现金的机器存在，但那些绘有水果图案的机器以及类似装置，让玩家每投入一枚硬币就有机会赢得一块口香糖或薄荷糖，这已不仅仅是一种无害的娱乐。它们是实打实的赌博工具，因为赢得的物品实际上可以在柜台兑换成现金。

**有利可图的非法勾当**

上海的老虎机每年攫取巨额资金并非神话。警方估计，公共租界内的老虎机数量约为300台，并称这是一个保守数字。据估计，这些机器每年的收入约为100万美元，其中一半落入机器所有者的口袋，另一半则归餐馆、酒吧或歌舞厅老板所有。

据计算，在法租界、公共租界和华界地区，约有1000台机器在运行，年收入超过400万美元。换句话说，老虎机已发展成为本市最大的非法勾当之一，每天为经营者带来的收入超过了卡洛斯·加西亚（Carlos Garcia）拥有的旧式“地狱赌场”轮盘赌的收入。

上海的大多数老虎机由辛迪加集团或个人拥有。许多小角色拥有三四台机器，放置在酒吧、餐馆和歌舞厅中。即使只有这么少数量的机器，一个人也能获得丰厚的收入，每月远超1000美元。本市有一人拥有72台机器组成的连锁网络，每台机器平均月收入为100美元，使其收入超过1万美元。在上海经济萧条之前，他的月收入曾高达2万美元。

大约四五年前，中国海关总署认为老虎机无非是一种机械窃贼，并禁止此类游戏机的进口。当时，整个城市只有约50台机器。此后，数量激增至一千台，甚至更多。警方将该数字视为最低限度。

**机器走私入境**

由此可见，向中国市场走私机器的生意对某些人来说是一本万利。为了使清理工作更具复杂性，如今上海有一些商行公然从事老虎机交易，以高价出售商品，并找到了现成的市场。

这些商行虽然愿意以五五分成的方式将机器放置在餐馆中，但更倾向于直接出售，因为利润回报快且周转量大。目前上海市场上大多数机器的价格在600至1000美元之间。据估计，本市在这些机器上的总投资约为70万美元。

美式老虎机首次大规模出现在上海是在1928年和1929年的冬季。在此之前，租界和法租界内虽有少量机器，但屈指可数。它们由少数酒吧老板个人拥有，用于赌雪茄和其他商品。

上海人所知的第一次公开服务发生在1928年末，当时一位来自美国的老虎机大亨带着18台机器抵达本港，并为一家纽约公司接受订单。此人在来到东方之前曾在欧洲经营，发现欧洲大陆各国坚决反对老虎机。在瑞士经历了一次痛苦的经历，导致他短暂入狱，且机器几乎被没收后，他前往上海。

他发现这座城市非常适合他的特定行业，没过几个月，他就将机器规模扩大到了二十多台。他前往广州和天津的一次行程提供了中国城市所需的大部分机器。由于他的活动，结果就是这些机器开始运作起来。

昨天无法得知目前的非法勾当究竟有多广泛。有人告诉我，许多场所内仍有大量机器。尚不清楚近期将采取何种措施迫使经销商移除机器。将机器从街头清除是一个问题；消除静安寺路134-O号轮盘赌下的赌博元素则是另一个问题。

（批注：2/6 14.）

THE CHINA PRESS, THURSDAY, JUNE 20, 1935.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / S. B. REGISTRY. / No. D 2708 / Date 21 / 6 / 35）

Slot Machine
Cleanup By
SMC Started

Machines Operated Only
As Gambling Devices
Are Ordered Removed

Owners Average $50
Weekly Profit On Unit

Slot machines, used for purely gambling purposes only, are again becoming a target for Settlement Police activities. Several local restaurant and cafe owners have just received letters from the police authorities demand that such machines be removed.

Questioned yesterday concerning these letters, police authorities stated that they were not making a drive on slot machines as a whole, but that they were carrying out a bit of routine that has been in progress for the past six or seven years. They added, however, that owners of machines who had received letters from the police demanding that such machines cease operations had simply been found to be breaking police regulations. They could not say, however, just how many machines would be forced out of action during the next few days.

A survey conducted by a CHINA Press reporter yesterday revealed that a good majority of the slot machines in the International Settlement are being operated solely as gambling devices. Only a few were found to be actual vendors of merchandise, such as chewing gum and that even these are not played for sticks of gum or candy, but for the 20 cent pieces that are paid out together with the merchandise.

The slot machine has been one of Shanghai's biggest "rackets" for the past seven or eight years and the amount of money that is poured into them every week runs well into five figures. It is difficult to calculate the number of machines in the entire city, let alone the International Settlement. It is safe to say that it runs well into the hundreds, officials say.

In making their sensational raid on slot machines two years ago, the New York police stated that such machines were merely mechanical thieves and that about 90 per cent of the money that went into them remained there. The machines used in Shanghai are of exactly the same type—as a matter of fact, they are made in the United States, and China today is one of the big markets for such devices.

Machines Earn $50 Weekly

Just how much money goes into Shanghai slot machines every year is hard to say, but the sum taken by every hundred machines can be computed fairly easily. Restaurant and cafe owners estimate that their machines are usually good for about $50 a week, half of which goes to the owner of the machine, the other half to the proprietor of the restaurant. For a hundred machines, the total is $20,000 a month, or a quarter of million dollars a year.

Settlement Police have been attempting to combat the slot machine evil in Shanghai ever since the bans went down on gambling shortly after the raid on the Bubbling Well Road wheel in 1928. Now they are renewing their efforts, and the man who can't produce a roll of mints or a package of chewing gum each time someone puts a 20-cent piece in his machine runs the risk of having to cut it off his list of assets.

（印章：上海公共租界工部局警务处 / 特别分部登记处。 / 编号 D 2708 / 日期 1935年6月21日）

工部局开始
清理老虎机

仅作为赌博设备
运行的机器被责令移除

业主平均每台机器
每周获利50美元

仅用于纯粹赌博目的的老虎机再次成为租界警方行动的目标。几位本地餐馆和咖啡馆老板刚刚收到警方当局的信函，要求移除此类机器。

昨日就这些信函询问警方当局时，警方表示，他们并非针对所有老虎机进行打击，而是在执行过去六七年来一直在进行的常规工作。然而，他们补充说，那些收到警方信函要求停止运营机器的业主，只是被发现违反了警务规章。不过，他们无法说明在未来几天内将有多少台机器被强制停用。

《字林西报》记者昨日进行的一项调查显示，公共租界内绝大多数老虎机仅作为赌博设备运行。只有少数被发现是真正的商品销售机，如口香糖，而且即使是这些机器，也不是为了赌口香糖棒或糖果，而是为了赌随商品一起支付的20分银币。

在过去七八年里，老虎机一直是上海最大的“非法勾当”之一，每周投入其中的资金数额高达五位数。很难计算整个城市乃至公共租界内的机器数量。官员们表示，可以肯定的是，数量多达数百台。

两年前，纽约警方在对老虎机进行轰动性突击搜查时表示，这些机器不过是机械窃贼，投入其中的资金约有90%留在了机器里。上海使用的机器属于完全相同的类型——事实上，它们是在美国制造的，而中国如今是此类设备的大市场之一。

机器每周赚取50美元

每年有多少资金流入上海的老虎机很难说，但每百台机器的收入可以比较容易地计算出来。餐馆和咖啡馆老板估计，他们的机器通常每周能带来约50美元的收益，其中一半归机器所有者，另一半归餐馆老板。对于一百台机器来说，总额为每月2万美元，即每年25万美元。

自1928年静安寺路轮盘赌案发生后不久颁布禁赌令以来，租界警方一直试图打击上海的老虎机弊病。现在他们正在重新努力，如果有人在每次向机器投入20分银币时不能拿出一卷薄荷糖或一包口香糖，他就面临着将其从资产列表中剔除的风险。

（手写签名）

On January 18, 1928 the Secretary of the Council received a letter from Mr. C.P. Holcomb, requesting on behalf of his client, permission to operate without a licence, Candy Vending Machines in the Settlement. 老虎机（中文报告档案 C.1388）

1928年1月18日，工部局秘书收到 C.P. Holcomb（音译）先生的一封信，代表其客户请求许可在租界内无执照经营糖果自动售货机。秘书于1928年2月3日回复称，工部局对在持照场所安装这些机器没有异议，且无需就这些机器缴纳特别执照费。然而，若将其安装在公共街道或其他公共财产上，则需事先获得工部局批准，并可能需缴纳地役权费用。

1929年1月26日，警务处处长致函税务司，指出某些人正准备进口大量赌博机器出售给中国人，并请求禁止自动老虎机、轮盘赌具及其他赌博用具的进口。信中强调，已有数台老虎机进口并投入运行。税务司于1929年3月11日回复称，已采纳警务处处长的建议，自1929年3月11日起，禁止所有形式的赌博器具、轮盘赌具等进口。然而，仅用于分发香烟、巧克力等的自动老虎机的进口仍将获准。

SUMMARY
Slot Machines (C.R.File C.1388)

On January 18, 1928 the Secretary of the Council
received a letter from Mr. C.P. Holcomb, requesting on
behalf of his client, permission to operate without a
licence, Candy Vending Machines in the Settlement.
The Secretary replied on February 3, 1928 stating that the
Council had no objection to the installation of the
machines in licensed premises and that no special licence
fee would be required in respect of the machines. Their
installation upon public streets or other public property
would, however, require the Council's approval in advance
and would, probably, be subject to an easement fee.

On January 26, 1929 the Commissioner of Police
addressed a letter to the Commissioner of Customs stating
that certain persons were about to import a large number
of gambling machines for sale to Chinese and requested that
the importation of automatic slot machines, roulette wheels
and other gambling paraphernalia be prohibited. It was
pointed out that several slot machinese had already been
imported and were in operation. The Commissioner of
Customs replied on March 11, 1929 to the effect that the
Commissioner of Police's suggestion had been adopted and
that all forms of gambling apparatus, roulette wheels, etc.
would be prohibited from March 11, 1929. The importation of
automatic slot machines used solely for the distribution of
cigarettes, chocolates, etc. would, however, still be
permitted.

About a year later it was found that many of the
machines known as "Mills Automatic Salesmen", "The Puritan
Bell", "Bell Fruit" and "Liberty Bell" which were installed
in numerous local Cabarets, Restaurants and other places,
did not have "candy" attachments. Others had "candy"

摘要
投币机（工部局档案 C.1388）

1928年1月18日，工部局秘书收到C.P. Holcomb先生代表其客户来信，请求允许在租界内无执照经营糖果自动售货机。秘书于1928年2月3日回复称，工部局对在持照场所安装此类机器不持异议，且无需就这些机器缴纳特别执照费。然而，若将其安装在公共街道或其他公共财产上，则需事先获得工部局批准，并可能需缴纳地役权费用。

1929年1月26日，警务处长致函海关税务司，指出某些人即将进口大量赌博机器出售给中国人，并要求禁止进口自动投币机、轮盘赌具及其他赌博用具。信中强调，已有数台投币机进口并投入运营。海关税务司于1929年3月11日回复称，已采纳警务处长的建议，自1929年3月11日起，禁止所有形式的赌博器具、轮盘等进口。然而，仅用于分发香烟、巧克力等的自动投币机仍允许进口。

约一年后，发现许多被称为“Mills Automatic Salesmen”、“The Puritan Bell”、“Bell Fruit”和“Liberty Bell”的机器，安装在众多本地歌舞厅、餐馆和其他场所，并没有“糖果”附件。另一些则有“糖果”

attachments, which in some cases were empty; these machines
could, however, still be used and a person inserting a 20d
piece would, if fortunate, receive a disc, which could
either be exchanged for cash or an article equivalent in
value to the disc received.

In view of the fact that most of the machines were
being used for gambling, the Commissioner of Police issued
instructions on January 29, 1929 that the operation of such
machines must cease forthwith. The proprietors of the
establishments concerned were warned accordingly and the
machines were withdrawn. This order did not effect those
machines used solely for the distribution of cigarettes,
chocolates, etc.

In 1930 it was discovered that the automatic slot
machines were again being used for gambling and on August
26, 1931 the Commissioner of Police issued instruction that
proprietors of premises having Fruit Machines which could
be used for gambling were to be warned against using the
machines for the purpose of gambling and that failure to
comply would render the proprietor of the premises liable
to prosecution. This warning had the desired effect.

Premises having slot machines are visited periodically
by the Police.

D. C. (Divisions)

SLOT MACHINES.
--------------

With reference to the attached file the following procedure
will be adopted.

Licensees of premises where Mills and Bell Fruit machines
are operated will be warned by Officers I/c. Police Stations in
person in the following sense.

（批：All files on slot machines on Cons. Reg. G. 1388.）

"In the opinion of the police the Fruit machine(s)
installed in your premises is (are) capable of being operated
as (a) gambling machine(s). The Council has informed an
interested party that so long as the operation of the
machines is restricted to the sale of candy and other goods
and does not constitute a lottery or other form of gambling
there is no objection to their installation in licensed
premises.

I am instructed by the Commissioner of Police to inform
you of this and to warn you that if gambling of this nature
is conducted on your premises you render yourself liable to
prosecution."

The warning will be conveyed verbally and a note of the
time, date and other particulars will be entered in the
occurrence book.

Thereafter the premises will be visited from time to time
and if the machines are still in operation the necessary evidence
will be collected with a view to prosecution of the licensee
after reference to the D. O. concerned and in consultation with
the Municipal Advocate. （批：Rw）

Premises on which a Jack-Pot machine has been in operation
and removed at the request of the police will also be kept under
observation and dealt with as in the preceding paragraph without
further warning.

R W Martin
Commissioner of Police.

投币机。
---

参照所附档案，将采取以下程序。

经营Mills和Bell Fruit机器的持照场所业主，将由各警察分局主管警官亲自向其发出如下内容的警告。

（批：所有关于投币机的档案均在领事注册档案 G. 1388中。）

“警方认为，贵场所安装的水果机具备作为赌博机器运营的能力。工部局已告知有关方面，只要机器的运营仅限于销售糖果和其他商品，不构成彩票或其他形式的赌博，工部局对其在持照场所的安装不持异议。

本人奉警务处长之命将此情况通知阁下，并警告阁下，若在贵场所进行此类赌博活动，阁下面临被起诉的风险。”

警告将以口头方式传达，并将时间、日期及其他细节记录在案情记录簿中。

此后，将不定期巡查该场所，如果机器仍在运营，将在咨询相关分区警官（D. O.）并与市法律顾问商议后，收集必要证据，以便对持照人提起诉讼。（批：Rw）

对于曾运营Jack-Pot机器并已应警方要求将其移除的场所，也将保持观察，并按前段规定处理，不再另行警告。

R W Martin
警务处长
